workingTitle: IceCube maps a fivefold neutrino gradient across the Milky Way
publicationStatus: IceCube Collaboration preprint first listed November 11, 2026; not yet peer reviewed
coreFacts: IceCube used 59,592 cascade events recorded from May 2011 to May 2021, spanning roughly 500 GeV to the PeV range.
At 5 TeV, the measured neutrino flux per solid angle within 30 degrees of the Galactic center is about five times that beyond 60 degrees Galactic longitude.
The inner and outer flux intervals are separated by about 2.5 standard deviations at 5 TeV.
The strongest tested segmentation gives 3.84 sigma before accounting for the eight tested schemes and 3.43 sigma after the trials correction.
The inner-Galaxy spectral index is 2.76 with asymmetric uncertainty, while the outer value is 3.13; the two remain compatible within current uncertainties.

In the region shared with LHAASO, the neutrino measurement is compatible with both diffuse-only and total gamma-ray flux under a fully hadronic conversion, so leptonic gamma-ray emission is not ruled out.
sourceStatus: Full primary paper and arXiv metadata read; all material numerical claims checked against the paper.
caveats: The flux contrast is suggestive rather than a definitive spatial detection, and statistical uncertainties dominate.
The gamma-ray comparison assumes a fully hadronic conversion and does not exclude leptonic emission.
